item.title: Industrial Alienation and the Logic of Scale
item.lead: In the dossier, the adult-tech industry emerges as an industrial process in which human unpredictability is replaced as much as possible by protocols, dashboards, and scripts.

blocks.text: The source describes a chain in which the personal front-end – profile, photo, conversation – is decoupled from the operational back-end. A user may believe they are communicating directly with a creator, while according to the described models, a team, manager, chatter, or automated system performs parts of the interaction. The essence of the critique thus lies not only in the content of the service, but in the invisibility of the production method.

This industrialization, according to the dossier, has multiple consequences. Conversations can be segmented into phases, objections can be categorized, vulnerabilities can be labeled, and revenue can be tracked per account or user. What was formerly a coincidental social encounter is then treated as a reproducible process with input, intervention, and measurable results.

For this, the source employs a number of recurring metaphors: factory, funnel, operations center, and machine. These metaphors emphasize standardization. The individual character of intimacy remains visually present, but the underlying organization can, according to the dossier, be centralized and professionalized.

For the philosophical framework, this is relevant because alienation is presented not only as alienation from labor, but also as alienation from human proximity. The creator becomes a production unit; the chatter becomes a sales function; the user becomes a revenue profile. The source perceives this as a shift from human meaning to system value.
